title: for / for-of / forEach
description: The three ways to walk an array: classic for, for…of, and forEach. Know when each one matters.

notes: forEach can NOT be exited early with `break` — use for / for…of when you need that.
forEach returns undefined; map returns a new array.
Avoid `for…in` on arrays — it gives keys as strings and includes inherited props.

questions.q: Which iteration cannot be exited early with `break`?
questions.explain: forEach takes a callback; `break` is only valid inside loop statements.
forEach is side-effect-only. Use map if you want a returned array.

questions.q: Which gives you the index as the second callback parameter?
questions.explain: Both pass (item, index, array) to the callback.

questions.q: For maximum speed on huge arrays, prefer:
questions.explain: Classic for avoids the iterator protocol. For most code the difference is negligible.

exercises.prompt: Sum the array with a for…of loop.
Print each element with its index using forEach.

L3.prompt: Write a function `sumArr(arr)` that returns the sum of all numbers. Then log `sumArr([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])`.
hints: Initialize an accumulator before the loop.
